newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia bourse adds 3 shares, drops 2 from SBI.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia bourse adds 3 shares, drops 2 from SBI.

text.p: Ljubljana stock exchange said on Monday it had added three new shares to the blue-chip SBI index and dropped two existing issues, taking the number of listings to 11, and had changed the calculation method.

The exchange said warehouse company BTC, pharmaceutical trader Salus and ordinary shares in bank Dolenjska Banka made their SBI debut on Monday while financial consultancies Dadas and Finmedia disappeared from the index.
"We changed the index so that it would better reflect the market," said Darko Torkar, head of trading at Ljubljana Stock Exchange.
The exchange also announced that in future the weight of each share in the index would depend upon its capitalisation.
"The new calculation has been introduced in a way to ensure continuity of the index value," Torkar said.

Apart from BTC, Salus and Dolenjska bank, shares of financial consultancy Nika, banks Probanka and SKB, food producers Kolinska and Droga, health resort operator Terme Catez, drug company Lek and trader Kovinotehna are in the SBI.
Shares included in the index represent some 80 percent of capitalisation of the main market of the Ljubljana bourse.
The bourse plans to review the index each May, September and January.
Currently, 25 shares are traded on the main market of the Ljubljana Stock Exchange.
